title: Billy Shaw on commissions and the union rules
summary: Shaw's fifteen percent arrangement, union limits on commissions, and the former 350-mile booking rule.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Managers, bookers and the business of getting work

blocks.x: Billy Shaw. He was to me one of the greatest agents that got in this business. He worked one of the big agencies; I think William Morris or something. But all he knew... He told me one day, he said, 'Walter, 15 percent is a lot of money.' He found out he could make 15 percent on one-nighters. He could make 20 percent, but if he took the 20 percent, then he had to allow for the expense of transportation and the union dues and so on. But he wrote out an agreement with the artist, that he would allow them the 5 percent to take care of that extra expense. So his 15 percent was clear. He didn't have to worry about nothin' else. And you think back... Of course, that was a long time ago. That was in the Fifties. But 15 percent right now is a lot of commission. And even in New York, when I was practicing... But the agent...but he was involved with the agencies, going to...
Not the New York... See, the New York percentage on booking is geared on the house workers. They're allowed 5 percent. But the agents went to the
states and told them they couldn't afford to book for 5 percent. And our union allows us 10 percent on locations...

And it allows 20 percent on one-nighters if you're getting double the scale. And then the union claims they deal from that 350, because as long as you was getting enough money and you could fly... That did away with the 350. Because years ago, you could only book artists 350 miles. But that all changed.
